title: 生態系のモデル比較
description: Lotka-Volterra, logistic prey and Holling type II fitted to the real Hudson's Bay Company hare and lynx pelt records of 1900-1920 with a hand-written RK4 and Nelder-Mead: residuals, AIC and BIC, a forecast of held-out years, and phase portraits far beyond the data. RK4 is checked with Lotka-Volterra's conserved quantity. Julia, charts in Vega-Lite.

using Printf

# The real record, bundled with the Card: the number of pelts the Hudson's Bay
# Company took each year. Pelts are a proxy for animals, not a census.
function main(ctx)
    years, lynx, hare = Int[], Float64[], Float64[]
    for line in eachline(joinpath(@__DIR__, "hudson-bay-lynx-hare.csv"))
        (startswith(line, "#") || startswith(line, "Year")) && continue
        y, l, h = split(line, ",")
        push!(years, parse(Int, y))
        push!(lynx, parse(Float64, l))
        push!(hare, parse(Float64, h))
    end
    println(@sprintf("%d years from %d to %d; largest hare %.1f, largest lynx %.1f (thousands of pelts)", length(years), years[1], years[end], maximum(hare), maximum(lynx)))
    output(ctx, "pelts", Dict("years" => years, "hare" => hare, "lynx" => lynx))

    rows = [Dict("year" => years[i], "pelts" => series[i], "species" => name)
            for (name, series) in (("ノウサギ（被食者）", hare), ("オオヤマネコ（捕食者）", lynx)) for i in eachindex(years)]
    display_vegalite(ctx, Dict(
        "\$schema" => "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v6.json",
        "background" => "white",
        "title" => Dict("anchor" => "start", "text" => "ハドソン湾会社の毛皮の記録（$(years[1])〜$(years[end]) 年、$(length(years)) 年分）",
                        "subtitle" => "実データ。出典: stan-dev/example-models（Howard 2009 の講義資料から）。個体数ではなく取引された毛皮の数"),
        "usermeta" => Dict("years" => years, "hare" => hare, "lynx" => lynx),
        "data" => Dict("values" => rows),
        "mark" => Dict("type" => "line", "strokeWidth" => 2, "point" => true),
        "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "year", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "年", "scale" => Dict("zero" => false), "axis" => Dict("format" => "d")),
                           "y" => Dict("field" => "pelts", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "毛皮の数（千枚）"),
                           "color" => Dict("field" => "species", "type" => "nominal", "title" => nothing,
                                           "scale" => Dict("domain" => ["ノウサギ（被食者）", "オオヤマネコ（捕食者）"], "range" => ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834"]),
                                           "legend" => Dict("orient" => "top-right")))))
end

# The models, the integrator and the optimizer of the demo (the same file is in
# fit, forecast, phase and check, so that each Card can be read and rerun alone).
using Random

# H: prey (hare), L: predator (lynx), in thousands of pelts; t in years.
lotka_volterra(H, L, p) = (p[1] * H - p[2] * H * L,
                           p[3] * H * L - p[4] * L)

logistic_prey(H, L, p) = (p[1] * H * (1 - H / p[5]) - p[2] * H * L,
                          p[3] * H * L - p[4] * L)

function holling_ii(H, L, p)
    eaten = p[2] * H / (1 + p[2] * p[6] * H) # per predator: saturates once handling takes the time
    return (p[1] * H * (1 - H / p[5]) - eaten * L,
            p[3] * eaten * L - p[4] * L)
end

# Each model: its right-hand side, and for each parameter a name and a range to start from.
const MODELS = [
    (name="ロトカ・ヴォルテラ", rhs=lotka_volterra,
     names=["a", "b", "c", "d"], low=[0.2, 0.005, 0.002, 0.2], high=[2.0, 0.1, 0.05, 2.0]),
    (name="被食者ロジスティック", rhs=logistic_prey,
     names=["a", "b", "c", "d", "K"], low=[0.2, 0.005, 0.002, 0.2, 50.0], high=[2.0, 0.1, 0.05, 2.0, 1000.0]),
    (name="ホリング II 型", rhs=holling_ii,
     names=["a", "b", "e", "d", "K", "h"], low=[0.2, 0.005, 0.05, 0.2, 50.0, 0.01], high=[2.0, 0.2, 1.0, 2.0, 1000.0, 2.0]),
]

# The classic fourth-order Runge-Kutta step.
function rk4_step(rhs::F, H, L, p, dt) where {F}
    k1 = rhs(H, L, p)
    k2 = rhs(H + dt / 2 * k1[1], L + dt / 2 * k1[2], p)
    k3 = rhs(H + dt / 2 * k2[1], L + dt / 2 * k2[2], p)
    k4 = rhs(H + dt * k3[1], L + dt * k3[2], p)
    return (H + dt / 6 * (k1[1] + 2k2[1] + 2k3[1] + k4[1]),
            L + dt / 6 * (k1[2] + 2k2[2] + 2k3[2] + k4[2]))
end

# The state at t = 0, 1/per_year, 2/per_year, ... up to `years`.
function simulate(rhs::F, p, H0, L0, years; per_year=1, dt=0.05) where {F}
    steps = round(Int, 1 / (per_year * dt))
    count = years * per_year + 1
    Hs = zeros(count)
    Ls = zeros(count)
    H, L = H0, L0
    Hs[1], Ls[1] = H, L
    for i in 2:count
        for _ in 1:steps
            H, L = rk4_step(rhs, H, L, p, dt)
        end
        Hs[i], Ls[i] = H, L
    end
    return Hs, Ls
end

# The sum of squared errors of log counts: pelts scatter by a factor, not by a fixed amount.
function log_squared_error(rhs::F, x, hare, lynx, dt) where {F}
    p = exp.(x)
    H, L = p[end - 1], p[end]
    total = 0.0
    for i in eachindex(hare)
        if i > 1
            for _ in 1:round(Int, 1 / dt)
                H, L = rk4_step(rhs, H, L, p, dt)
            end
        end
        (H > 1e-6 && L > 1e-6 && H < 1e7 && L < 1e7) || return 1e9
        total += (log(hare[i]) - log(H))^2 + (log(lynx[i]) - log(L))^2
    end
    return total
end

# Nelder-Mead on the logarithms of the parameters, so that they stay positive.
function nelder_mead(f, start; size=0.3, max_evaluations=6000, tolerance=1e-9)
    n = length(start)
    points = [copy(start) for _ in 1:n+1]
    for i in 1:n
        points[i + 1][i] += size
    end
    values = f.(points)
    evaluations = n + 1
    while evaluations < max_evaluations
        order = sortperm(values)
        points, values = points[order], values[order]
        values[end] - values[1] < tolerance && break
        centre = sum(points[1:n]) / n
        reflected = centre + (centre - points[end])
        fr = f(reflected)
        evaluations += 1
        if fr < values[1]
            expanded = centre + 2 * (centre - points[end])
            fe = f(expanded)
            evaluations += 1
            points[end], values[end] = fe < fr ? (expanded, fe) : (reflected, fr)
        elseif fr < values[n]
            points[end], values[end] = reflected, fr
        else
            contracted = centre + 0.5 * ((fr < values[end] ? reflected : points[end]) - centre)
            fc = f(contracted)
            evaluations += 1
            if fc < min(fr, values[end])
                points[end], values[end] = contracted, fc
            else
                for i in 2:n+1
                    points[i] = points[1] + 0.5 * (points[i] - points[1])
                    values[i] = f(points[i])
                end
                evaluations += n
            end
        end
    end
    best = argmin(values)
    return points[best], values[best]
end

# Starts Nelder-Mead from `restarts` random points, and restarts it from its best
# result (a simplex can collapse early). `agreeing`: how many starts ended within
# 1% of the best, which says how rugged the error surface is.
function fit_model(model, hare, lynx, restarts, rng, dt)
    f(x) = log_squared_error(model.rhs, x, hare, lynx, dt)
    lows = vcat(model.low, [hare[1] / 2, lynx[1] / 2])
    highs = vcat(model.high, [hare[1] * 2, lynx[1] * 2])
    ends = Float64[]
    best_x, best_error = Float64[], Inf
    for _ in 1:restarts
        start = [log(l) + rand(rng) * (log(h) - log(l)) for (l, h) in zip(lows, highs)]
        x, e = nelder_mead(f, start)
        x, e = nelder_mead(f, x; size=0.1)
        push!(ends, e)
        if e < best_error
            best_x, best_error = x, e
        end
    end
    return (parameters=exp.(best_x), error=best_error, agreeing=count(<=(best_error * 1.01), ends))
end

using Printf
include("ecology.jl")

# Fits each model to the record up to `fit_until` and scores it. The noise level
# is estimated too, so it counts as one more parameter in AIC and BIC.
function main(ctx)
    m = input(ctx, "pelts")
    years = Int.(m["years"])
    hare, lynx = Float64.(m["hare"]), Float64.(m["lynx"])
    until = Int(ctx.params["fit_until"])
    restarts = Int(ctx.params["restarts"])
    dt = ctx.params["dt"]
    used = findall(<=(until), years)
    rng = Xoshiro(ctx.params["seed"])
    n = 2 * length(used)

    results = Dict{String,Any}[]
    curves = Dict{String,Any}[]
    span = years[end] - years[1]
    for model in MODELS
        fit = fit_model(model, hare[used], lynx[used], restarts, rng, dt)
        p = fit.parameters
        k = length(p) + 1
        aic = n * log(fit.error / n) + 2k
        aicc = aic + 2k * (k + 1) / (n - k - 1)
        bic = n * log(fit.error / n) + k * log(n)
        Hs, Ls = simulate(model.rhs, p, p[end - 1], p[end], span; per_year=4, dt)
        println(@sprintf("%s: error %.4f, k = %d, AIC %.2f, AICc %.2f, BIC %.2f, %d of %d starts agree", model.name, fit.error, k, aic, aicc, bic, fit.agreeing, restarts))
        println("  ", join((@sprintf("%s = %.4g", name, v) for (name, v) in zip(vcat(model.names, ["H0", "L0"]), p)), ", "))
        push!(results, Dict("name" => model.name, "parameter_names" => vcat(model.names, ["H0", "L0"]), "parameters" => p,
                            "sse" => fit.error, "n" => n, "k" => k, "aic" => aic, "aicc" => aicc, "bic" => bic,
                            "rmse_log" => sqrt(fit.error / n), "agreeing" => fit.agreeing, "restarts" => restarts))
        for i in eachindex(Hs)
            year = years[1] + (i - 1) / 4
            push!(curves, Dict("year" => year, "pelts" => round(Hs[i]; digits=2), "species" => "ノウサギ", "model" => model.name))
            push!(curves, Dict("year" => year, "pelts" => round(Ls[i]; digits=2), "species" => "オオヤマネコ", "model" => model.name))
        end
    end
    output(ctx, "fits", Dict("fit_until" => until, "models" => results))

    observed = [Dict("year" => years[i], "pelts" => series[i], "species" => name)
                for (name, series) in (("ノウサギ", hare), ("オオヤマネコ", lynx)) for i in eachindex(years)]
    names = [model.name for model in MODELS]
    colors = Dict("domain" => names, "range" => ["#2a78d6", "#1baf7a", "#eb6834"])
    dashes = Dict("domain" => names, "range" => [[1, 0], [1, 0], [5, 4]]) # the fits can coincide
    holling = results[3]["parameters"]
    panel(species, title)= Dict("width" => 640, "height" => 140,
        "layer" => [
            Dict("data" => Dict("values" => filter(r -> r["species"] == species, curves)), "mark" => Dict("type" => "line", "strokeWidth" => 1.8),
                 "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "year", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "年", "scale" => Dict("zero" => false, "nice" => false), "axis" => Dict("format" => "d")),
                                    "y" => Dict("field" => "pelts", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => title),
                                    "color" => Dict("field" => "model", "type" => "nominal", "title" => "モデル", "scale" => colors),
                                    "strokeDash" => Dict("field" => "model", "type" => "nominal", "title" => "モデル", "scale" => dashes))),
            Dict("data" => Dict("values" => filter(r -> r["species"] == species, observed)), "mark" => Dict("type" => "point", "filled" => true, "size" => 34, "color" => "#111111"),
                 "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "year", "type" => "quantitative"), "y" => Dict("field" => "pelts", "type" => "quantitative"))),
        ])
    display_vegalite(ctx, Dict(
        "\$schema" => "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v6.json",
        "background" => "white",
        "title" => Dict("text" => "3 つのモデルを $(years[1])〜$(until) 年の記録に当てはめる",
                        "subtitle" => [
                            "黒い点が毛皮の記録（千枚）。線は各モデルの最良の解（対数の誤差を最小化、$(restarts) 通りの初期値から）",
                            @sprintf("ホリング II 型の処理時間 h = %.2g、環境収容力 K = %.0f。h が 0 に近く K が大きいなら、足した項はほとんど使われていない", holling[6], holling[5]),
                        ]),
        "usermeta" => Dict("fits" => results),
        "vconcat" => [panel("ノウサギ", "ノウサギ（千枚）"), panel("オオヤマネコ", "オオヤマネコ（千枚）")]))
end

# The models, the integrator and the optimizer of the demo (the same file is in
# fit, forecast, phase and check, so that each Card can be read and rerun alone).
using Random

# H: prey (hare), L: predator (lynx), in thousands of pelts; t in years.
lotka_volterra(H, L, p) = (p[1] * H - p[2] * H * L,
                           p[3] * H * L - p[4] * L)

logistic_prey(H, L, p) = (p[1] * H * (1 - H / p[5]) - p[2] * H * L,
                          p[3] * H * L - p[4] * L)

function holling_ii(H, L, p)
    eaten = p[2] * H / (1 + p[2] * p[6] * H) # per predator: saturates once handling takes the time
    return (p[1] * H * (1 - H / p[5]) - eaten * L,
            p[3] * eaten * L - p[4] * L)
end

# Each model: its right-hand side, and for each parameter a name and a range to start from.
const MODELS = [
    (name="ロトカ・ヴォルテラ", rhs=lotka_volterra,
     names=["a", "b", "c", "d"], low=[0.2, 0.005, 0.002, 0.2], high=[2.0, 0.1, 0.05, 2.0]),
    (name="被食者ロジスティック", rhs=logistic_prey,
     names=["a", "b", "c", "d", "K"], low=[0.2, 0.005, 0.002, 0.2, 50.0], high=[2.0, 0.1, 0.05, 2.0, 1000.0]),
    (name="ホリング II 型", rhs=holling_ii,
     names=["a", "b", "e", "d", "K", "h"], low=[0.2, 0.005, 0.05, 0.2, 50.0, 0.01], high=[2.0, 0.2, 1.0, 2.0, 1000.0, 2.0]),
]

# The classic fourth-order Runge-Kutta step.
function rk4_step(rhs::F, H, L, p, dt) where {F}
    k1 = rhs(H, L, p)
    k2 = rhs(H + dt / 2 * k1[1], L + dt / 2 * k1[2], p)
    k3 = rhs(H + dt / 2 * k2[1], L + dt / 2 * k2[2], p)
    k4 = rhs(H + dt * k3[1], L + dt * k3[2], p)
    return (H + dt / 6 * (k1[1] + 2k2[1] + 2k3[1] + k4[1]),
            L + dt / 6 * (k1[2] + 2k2[2] + 2k3[2] + k4[2]))
end

# The state at t = 0, 1/per_year, 2/per_year, ... up to `years`.
function simulate(rhs::F, p, H0, L0, years; per_year=1, dt=0.05) where {F}
    steps = round(Int, 1 / (per_year * dt))
    count = years * per_year + 1
    Hs = zeros(count)
    Ls = zeros(count)
    H, L = H0, L0
    Hs[1], Ls[1] = H, L
    for i in 2:count
        for _ in 1:steps
            H, L = rk4_step(rhs, H, L, p, dt)
        end
        Hs[i], Ls[i] = H, L
    end
    return Hs, Ls
end

# The sum of squared errors of log counts: pelts scatter by a factor, not by a fixed amount.
function log_squared_error(rhs::F, x, hare, lynx, dt) where {F}
    p = exp.(x)
    H, L = p[end - 1], p[end]
    total = 0.0
    for i in eachindex(hare)
        if i > 1
            for _ in 1:round(Int, 1 / dt)
                H, L = rk4_step(rhs, H, L, p, dt)
            end
        end
        (H > 1e-6 && L > 1e-6 && H < 1e7 && L < 1e7) || return 1e9
        total += (log(hare[i]) - log(H))^2 + (log(lynx[i]) - log(L))^2
    end
    return total
end

# Nelder-Mead on the logarithms of the parameters, so that they stay positive.
function nelder_mead(f, start; size=0.3, max_evaluations=6000, tolerance=1e-9)
    n = length(start)
    points = [copy(start) for _ in 1:n+1]
    for i in 1:n
        points[i + 1][i] += size
    end
    values = f.(points)
    evaluations = n + 1
    while evaluations < max_evaluations
        order = sortperm(values)
        points, values = points[order], values[order]
        values[end] - values[1] < tolerance && break
        centre = sum(points[1:n]) / n
        reflected = centre + (centre - points[end])
        fr = f(reflected)
        evaluations += 1
        if fr < values[1]
            expanded = centre + 2 * (centre - points[end])
            fe = f(expanded)
            evaluations += 1
            points[end], values[end] = fe < fr ? (expanded, fe) : (reflected, fr)
        elseif fr < values[n]
            points[end], values[end] = reflected, fr
        else
            contracted = centre + 0.5 * ((fr < values[end] ? reflected : points[end]) - centre)
            fc = f(contracted)
            evaluations += 1
            if fc < min(fr, values[end])
                points[end], values[end] = contracted, fc
            else
                for i in 2:n+1
                    points[i] = points[1] + 0.5 * (points[i] - points[1])
                    values[i] = f(points[i])
                end
                evaluations += n
            end
        end
    end
    best = argmin(values)
    return points[best], values[best]
end

# Starts Nelder-Mead from `restarts` random points, and restarts it from its best
# result (a simplex can collapse early). `agreeing`: how many starts ended within
# 1% of the best, which says how rugged the error surface is.
function fit_model(model, hare, lynx, restarts, rng, dt)
    f(x) = log_squared_error(model.rhs, x, hare, lynx, dt)
    lows = vcat(model.low, [hare[1] / 2, lynx[1] / 2])
    highs = vcat(model.high, [hare[1] * 2, lynx[1] * 2])
    ends = Float64[]
    best_x, best_error = Float64[], Inf
    for _ in 1:restarts
        start = [log(l) + rand(rng) * (log(h) - log(l)) for (l, h) in zip(lows, highs)]
        x, e = nelder_mead(f, start)
        x, e = nelder_mead(f, x; size=0.1)
        push!(ends, e)
        if e < best_error
            best_x, best_error = x, e
        end
    end
    return (parameters=exp.(best_x), error=best_error, agreeing=count(<=(best_error * 1.01), ends))
end

using Printf
include("ecology.jl")

# The test AIC cannot give: fit only the early years, then compare each model's
# simulation with the years it has not seen.
function main(ctx)
    m = input(ctx, "pelts")
    years = Int.(m["years"])
    hare, lynx = Float64.(m["hare"]), Float64.(m["lynx"])
    until = Int(ctx.params["fit_until"])
    restarts = Int(ctx.params["restarts"])
    dt = ctx.params["dt"]
    used = findall(<=(until), years)
    held = findall(>(until), years)
    isempty(held) && error("fit_until must leave at least one year out")
    rng = Xoshiro(ctx.params["seed"])

    span = years[end] - years[1]
    results = Dict{String,Any}[]
    curves = Dict{String,Any}[]
    for model in MODELS
        fit = fit_model(model, hare[used], lynx[used], restarts, rng, dt)
        p = fit.parameters
        Hs, Ls = simulate(model.rhs, p, p[end - 1], p[end], span; dt)
        errors = vcat(log.(hare[held]) .- log.(Hs[held]), log.(lynx[held]) .- log.(Ls[held]))
        rmse = sqrt(sum(abs2, errors) / length(errors))
        in_sample = sqrt(fit.error / (2 * length(used)))
        println(@sprintf("%s: RMSE of log counts %.3f on the fitted years, %.3f on the held-out years", model.name, in_sample, rmse))
        push!(results, Dict("name" => model.name, "rmse_fit" => in_sample, "rmse_heldout" => rmse, "parameters" => p,
                            "hare" => Hs, "lynx" => Ls))
        fine_H, fine_L = simulate(model.rhs, p, p[end - 1], p[end], span; per_year=4, dt)
        for i in eachindex(fine_H)
            year = years[1] + (i - 1) / 4
            push!(curves, Dict("year" => year, "pelts" => round(fine_H[i]; digits=2), "species" => "ノウサギ", "model" => model.name))
            push!(curves, Dict("year" => year, "pelts" => round(fine_L[i]; digits=2), "species" => "オオヤマネコ", "model" => model.name))
        end
    end
    output(ctx, "forecast", Dict("fit_until" => until, "last_year" => years[end],
                                 "names" => [r["name"] for r in results], "rmse_fit" => [r["rmse_fit"] for r in results], "rmse_heldout" => [r["rmse_heldout"] for r in results]))

    observed = [Dict("year" => years[i], "pelts" => series[i], "species" => name)
                for (name, series) in (("ノウサギ", hare), ("オオヤマネコ", lynx)) for i in eachindex(years)]
    names = [model.name for model in MODELS]
    colors = Dict("domain" => names, "range" => ["#2a78d6", "#1baf7a", "#eb6834"])

# The models, the integrator and the optimizer of the demo (the same file is in
# fit, forecast, phase and check, so that each Card can be read and rerun alone).
using Random

# H: prey (hare), L: predator (lynx), in thousands of pelts; t in years.
lotka_volterra(H, L, p) = (p[1] * H - p[2] * H * L,
                           p[3] * H * L - p[4] * L)

logistic_prey(H, L, p) = (p[1] * H * (1 - H / p[5]) - p[2] * H * L,
                          p[3] * H * L - p[4] * L)

function holling_ii(H, L, p)
    eaten = p[2] * H / (1 + p[2] * p[6] * H) # per predator: saturates once handling takes the time
    return (p[1] * H * (1 - H / p[5]) - eaten * L,
            p[3] * eaten * L - p[4] * L)
end

# Each model: its right-hand side, and for each parameter a name and a range to start from.
const MODELS = [
    (name="ロトカ・ヴォルテラ", rhs=lotka_volterra,
     names=["a", "b", "c", "d"], low=[0.2, 0.005, 0.002, 0.2], high=[2.0, 0.1, 0.05, 2.0]),
    (name="被食者ロジスティック", rhs=logistic_prey,
     names=["a", "b", "c", "d", "K"], low=[0.2, 0.005, 0.002, 0.2, 50.0], high=[2.0, 0.1, 0.05, 2.0, 1000.0]),
    (name="ホリング II 型", rhs=holling_ii,
     names=["a", "b", "e", "d", "K", "h"], low=[0.2, 0.005, 0.05, 0.2, 50.0, 0.01], high=[2.0, 0.2, 1.0, 2.0, 1000.0, 2.0]),
]

# The classic fourth-order Runge-Kutta step.
function rk4_step(rhs::F, H, L, p, dt) where {F}
    k1 = rhs(H, L, p)
    k2 = rhs(H + dt / 2 * k1[1], L + dt / 2 * k1[2], p)
    k3 = rhs(H + dt / 2 * k2[1], L + dt / 2 * k2[2], p)
    k4 = rhs(H + dt * k3[1], L + dt * k3[2], p)
    return (H + dt / 6 * (k1[1] + 2k2[1] + 2k3[1] + k4[1]),
            L + dt / 6 * (k1[2] + 2k2[2] + 2k3[2] + k4[2]))
end

# The state at t = 0, 1/per_year, 2/per_year, ... up to `years`.
function simulate(rhs::F, p, H0, L0, years; per_year=1, dt=0.05) where {F}
    steps = round(Int, 1 / (per_year * dt))
    count = years * per_year + 1
    Hs = zeros(count)
    Ls = zeros(count)
    H, L = H0, L0
    Hs[1], Ls[1] = H, L
    for i in 2:count
        for _ in 1:steps
            H, L = rk4_step(rhs, H, L, p, dt)
        end
        Hs[i], Ls[i] = H, L
    end
    return Hs, Ls
end

# The sum of squared errors of log counts: pelts scatter by a factor, not by a fixed amount.
function log_squared_error(rhs::F, x, hare, lynx, dt) where {F}
    p = exp.(x)
    H, L = p[end - 1], p[end]
    total = 0.0
    for i in eachindex(hare)
        if i > 1
            for _ in 1:round(Int, 1 / dt)
                H, L = rk4_step(rhs, H, L, p, dt)
            end
        end
        (H > 1e-6 && L > 1e-6 && H < 1e7 && L < 1e7) || return 1e9
        total += (log(hare[i]) - log(H))^2 + (log(lynx[i]) - log(L))^2
    end
    return total
end

# Nelder-Mead on the logarithms of the parameters, so that they stay positive.
function nelder_mead(f, start; size=0.3, max_evaluations=6000, tolerance=1e-9)
    n = length(start)
    points = [copy(start) for _ in 1:n+1]
    for i in 1:n
        points[i + 1][i] += size
    end
    values = f.(points)
    evaluations = n + 1
    while evaluations < max_evaluations
        order = sortperm(values)
        points, values = points[order], values[order]
        values[end] - values[1] < tolerance && break
        centre = sum(points[1:n]) / n
        reflected = centre + (centre - points[end])
        fr = f(reflected)
        evaluations += 1
        if fr < values[1]
            expanded = centre + 2 * (centre - points[end])
            fe = f(expanded)
            evaluations += 1
            points[end], values[end] = fe < fr ? (expanded, fe) : (reflected, fr)
        elseif fr < values[n]
            points[end], values[end] = reflected, fr
        else
            contracted = centre + 0.5 * ((fr < values[end] ? reflected : points[end]) - centre)
            fc = f(contracted)
            evaluations += 1
            if fc < min(fr, values[end])
                points[end], values[end] = contracted, fc
            else
                for i in 2:n+1
                    points[i] = points[1] + 0.5 * (points[i] - points[1])
                    values[i] = f(points[i])
                end
                evaluations += n
            end
        end
    end
    best = argmin(values)
    return points[best], values[best]
end

# Starts Nelder-Mead from `restarts` random points, and restarts it from its best
# result (a simplex can collapse early). `agreeing`: how many starts ended within
# 1% of the best, which says how rugged the error surface is.
function fit_model(model, hare, lynx, restarts, rng, dt)
    f(x) = log_squared_error(model.rhs, x, hare, lynx, dt)
    lows = vcat(model.low, [hare[1] / 2, lynx[1] / 2])
    highs = vcat(model.high, [hare[1] * 2, lynx[1] * 2])
    ends = Float64[]
    best_x, best_error = Float64[], Inf
    for _ in 1:restarts
        start = [log(l) + rand(rng) * (log(h) - log(l)) for (l, h) in zip(lows, highs)]
        x, e = nelder_mead(f, start)
        x, e = nelder_mead(f, x; size=0.1)
        push!(ends, e)
        if e < best_error
            best_x, best_error = x, e
        end
    end
    return (parameters=exp.(best_x), error=best_error, agreeing=count(<=(best_error * 1.01), ends))
end

using Printf
include("ecology.jl")

# Similar fits over 21 years can mean different futures: a closed orbit, a spiral
# into a fixed point or a limit cycle. Each fit is run far beyond the data.
function main(ctx)
    f = input(ctx, "fits")
    years = Int(ctx.params["years"])
    dt = ctx.params["dt"]
    rows = Dict{String,Any}[]
    ends = Dict{String,Any}[]
    swing = Dict{String,Float64}()
    for (model, m) in zip(MODELS, f["models"])
        p = Float64.(m["parameters"])
        per_year = 8
        Hs, Ls = simulate(model.rhs, p, p[end - 1], p[end], years; per_year, dt)
        # The size of the last cycles, in hare: a settled orbit keeps it, a spiral loses it.
        tail = max(1, length(Hs) - per_year * 30):length(Hs)
        swing[model.name] = maximum(Hs[tail]) - minimum(Hs[tail])
        println(@sprintf("%s: over the last 30 of %d simulated years the hare swings by %.2f, ending at H = %.2f, L = %.2f", model.name, years, swing[model.name], Hs[end], Ls[end]))
        for i in eachindex(Hs)
            push!(rows, Dict("H" => round(Hs[i]; digits=2), "L" => round(Ls[i]; digits=2), "t" => i, "model" => model.name,
                             "phase" => i <= per_year * 21 ? "記録と同じ 21 年" : "その後の $(years - 21) 年"))
        end
    end
    names = [model.name for model in MODELS]
    display_vegalite(ctx, Dict(
        "\$schema" => "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v6.json",
        "background" => "white",
        "title" => Dict("text" => "似た当てはめでも、先の動きは別物になりうる",
                        "subtitle" => "各モデルの最良の解を $(years) 年先まで延ばした相図。データのない範囲で、これは予言ではなく式の性質"),
        "usermeta" => Dict("swing" => swing),
        "data" => Dict("values" => rows),
        "facet" => Dict("field" => "model", "type" => "nominal", "sort" => names, "title" => nothing, "header" => Dict("labelFontSize" => 12)),
        "columns" => 3,
        "spec" => Dict("width" => 230, "height" => 240,
                       "mark" => Dict("type" => "line", "strokeWidth" => 1.3, "clip" => true),
                       "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "H", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "ノウサギ H（千枚）"),
                                          "y" => Dict("field" => "L", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "オオヤマネコ L（千枚）"),
                                          "order" => Dict("field" => "t", "type" => "quantitative"),
                                          "color" => Dict("field" => "phase", "type" => "nominal", "title" => nothing,
                                                          "scale" => Dict("domain" => ["記録と同じ 21 年", "その後の $(years - 21) 年"], "range" => ["#eb6834", "#2a78d6"]),
                                                          "legend" => Dict("orient" => "bottom"))))))
end

# The classic fourth-order Runge-Kutta step.
function rk4_step(rhs::F, H, L, p, dt) where {F}
    k1 = rhs(H, L, p)
    k2 = rhs(H + dt / 2 * k1[1], L + dt / 2 * k1[2], p)
    k3 = rhs(H + dt / 2 * k2[1], L + dt / 2 * k2[2], p)
    k4 = rhs(H + dt * k3[1], L + dt * k3[2], p)
    return (H + dt / 6 * (k1[1] + 2k2[1] + 2k3[1] + k4[1]),
            L + dt / 6 * (k1[2] + 2k2[2] + 2k3[2] + k4[2]))

# The state at t = 0, 1/per_year, 2/per_year, ... up to `years`.
function simulate(rhs::F, p, H0, L0, years; per_year=1, dt=0.05) where {F}
    steps = round(Int, 1 / (per_year * dt))
    count = years * per_year + 1
    Hs = zeros(count)
    Ls = zeros(count)
    H, L = H0, L0
    Hs[1], Ls[1] = H, L
    for i in 2:count
        for _ in 1:steps
            H, L = rk4_step(rhs, H, L, p, dt)

# The sum of squared errors of log counts: pelts scatter by a factor, not by a fixed amount.
function log_squared_error(rhs::F, x, hare, lynx, dt) where {F}

# Nelder-Mead on the logarithms of the parameters, so that they stay positive.

    points = [copy(start) for _ in 1:n+1]

            fe = f(expanded)
            evaluations += 1

            points[end], values[end] = reflected, fr

                    points[i] = points[1] + 0.5 * (points[i] - points[1])

# result (a simplex can collapse early). `agreeing`: how many starts ended within
# 1% of the best, which says how rugged the error surface is.
function fit_model(model, hare, lynx, restarts, rng, dt)
    f(x) = log_squared_error(model.rhs, x, hare, lynx, dt)
    lows = vcat(model.low, [hare[1] / 2, lynx[1] / 2])
    highs = vcat(model.high, [hare[1] * 2, lynx[1] * 2])

    best_x, best_error = Float64[], Inf
    for _ in 1:restarts
        start = [log(l) + rand(rng) * (log(h) - log(l)) for (l, h) in zip(lows, highs)]
        x, e = nelder_mead(f, start)
        x, e = nelder_mead(f, x; size=0.1)
        push!(ends, e)
        if e < best_error
            best_x, best_error = x, e
        end
    end

using Printf
include("ecology.jl")

# Lotka-Volterra has a conserved quantity, so the integrator can be tested without
# any data: V = c H - d log H + b L - a log L stays constant along an exact orbit.
conserved(H, L, p) = p[3] * H - p[4] * log(H) + p[2] * L - p[1] * log(L)

function drift(p, years, dt)
    H, L = p[end - 1], p[end]
    start = conserved(H, L, p)
    worst = 0.0
    for _ in 1:round(Int, years / dt)
        H, L = rk4_step(lotka_volterra, H, L, p, dt)
        worst = max(worst, abs(conserved(H, L, p) - start))
    end
    return worst
end

# Bob Carpenter's Stan case study "Predator-Prey Population Dynamics" fits the same
# model to the same 21 years by Bayesian inference: posterior median and 10-90% interval.
const STAN = (a=(0.542, 0.465, 0.630), b=(0.027, 0.022, 0.033), c=(0.024, 0.020, 0.029), d=(0.797, 0.692, 0.926),
              H0=(33.908, 30.415, 37.630), L0=(5.912, 5.273, 6.614))

function main(ctx)
    f = input(ctx, "fits")
    years = Int(ctx.params["years"])
    steps = Float64.(ctx.params["dt"])
    lv = f["models"][1]
    p = Float64.(lv["parameters"])
    rows = Vector{Any}[]

    previous = NaN
    for dt in steps
        d = drift(p, years, dt)
        verdict = isnan(previous) ? "基準" : @sprintf("半分の刻みで 1/%.1f（4 次なら 1/16 に近づく）", previous / d)
        push!(rows, [@sprintf("RK4 の保存量 V のずれ、dt = %g 年、%d 年間", dt, years), @sprintf("%.2e", d), "0", verdict])
        isnan(previous) || previous / d > 8 || error(@sprintf("halving dt shrank the drift only %.1f times", previous / d))
        previous = d
    end
    d = drift(p, years, 0.05)
    d < 1e-3 || error("the drift at the demo's dt is $d")

    if f["fit_until"] == 1920
        for (name, value) in zip(lv["parameter_names"], p)
            median, low, high = getfield(STAN, Symbol(name))
            inside = low <= value <= high
            push!(rows, ["LV の $(name) と Stan の事例研究", @sprintf("%.3f", value), @sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", median, low, high),
                         inside ? "10〜90% の範囲内" : "範囲外"])
        end
    else
        push!(rows, ["LV と Stan の事例研究", "fit_until = $(f["fit_until"])", "1900〜1920 年の値", "全期間でないので比べない"])
    end
    display_table(ctx, ["確かめたこと", "値", "基準", "判定"], rows)
end

notes.html:
生態系のモデル比較

ハドソン湾会社の毛皮の記録（実データ、1900〜1920 年、出典: stan-dev/example-models、Howard 2009 の講義資料から）に、3 つの捕食・被食モデルを当てはめます。

LV: H˙=aH−bHL,  L˙=cHL−dL\text{LV: } \dot H=aH-bHL,\ \ \dot L=cHL-dL 被食者ロジスティック: aH→aH(1−H/K)\text{被食者ロジスティック: } aH\to aH(1-H/K) ホリング II 型: bH→bH1+bhH\text{ホリング II 型: } bH\to \frac{bH}{1+bhH}

誤差は対数の二乗和で、同じ分散の正規ノイズを仮定して AIC=nlog⁡(SSE/n)+2k\mathrm{AIC}=n\log(\mathrm{SSE}/n)+2k で比べます。

AIC が良くても、その仕組みが正しいとは言えません。AIC は手元の式の中での相対的な順位を示すだけで、残差の自己相関も無視しています。また毛皮の数は個体数ではなく、罠の数や毛皮の値段、捕らえやすさ（飢えた個体は罠にかかりやすい）に左右される代理の値です。

forecast の fit_until で残す年を、fit の restarts で初期値の数を変えて試せます。
